principles.name: No wall of shame
principles.rule: Records should describe evidence, incentives, systems, and consequences without treating failure as humiliation.

principles.name: Dignity of harmed people
principles.rule: Engineering/medical disaster records must not turn victims, families, or survivors into rhetorical props.

principles.name: Living researcher care
principles.rule: Unpublished negative results, abandoned studies, and private lab failures require extra care; avoid naming individuals unless source, consent, public interest, and context justify it.

principles.name: Hindsight bias warning
principles.rule: Records should state what was knowable at the time, not only what is obvious afterward.

principles.name: Sensitive-domain review
principles.rule: Claims involving stigmatized groups, medicine, law, national security, or traumatic deaths require a sensitivity class and extra source scrutiny.

principles.name: Private material boundary
principles.rule: Private correspondence, Slack/Discord/email/lab notes, and confidential studies should be represented only when lawful, ethical, and necessary.

principles.name: No premature pedagogy
principles.rule: Do not turn candidate or seed-only examples into teaching material until sources, status, uncertainty, and ethical framing have been reviewed.

entries.title: Fatality case handling
entries.rule: For records involving deaths or severe harm, use aggregate casualty context unless individual naming is necessary, sourced, and ethically justified. Avoid spectacle and keep causal focus on systems, decisions, and evidence.

entries.title: No programmer-blame anecdotes
entries.rule: Software-related engineering failures must preserve system context: requirements, interfaces, tests, operational assumptions, organizational transfer, and review processes. Do not collapse cases into 'someone wrote bad code'.

entries.risk: Medical negative-result records can be misread as patient advice, blanket treatment rejection, or retrospective shaming of clinicians and investigators.
entries.handling_rule: Each medical record must state population, intervention, dose/route when known, endpoint, benefits preserved, harms preserved, and scope cautions. The cube does not provide medical advice.

entries.risk: Genealogy records can turn into prestige lineage, erase informal or marginalized transmission, or mistake formal ancestry for influence.
entries.handling_rule: Every genealogy relation must carry relation type, confidence, source, and a non-equivalence warning when appropriate; absence from a genealogy infrastructure is not evidence of absence.

entries.risk: ALPAC/Lighthill-style records can be weaponized as anti-field slogans or presentist mockery of researchers working under older constraints.
entries.handling_rule: Preserve evaluator criteria, recommendations, response scenes, revival possibilities, and causal uncertainty. Do not encode evaluator criticism as timeless field failure.

entries.risk: High-sensitivity engineering records can become blame spectacle, management folklore, or trauma content detached from the people killed and injured.
entries.handling_rule: Keep event severity factual and minimal; default to system/organization-level analysis; avoid unnecessary personal detail; ensure pattern records cite source-backed incident records and preserve uncertainty.

entries.risk: Public de-identified safety reports can be re-identified when combined with time, location, operator, or incident-specific details; confidential-reporting systems can also be misused as blame archives.
entries.handling_rule: Rev0007 promotes only the infrastructure pages. Do not import individual reports until a privacy protocol exists; when imported later, preserve sanitization, aggregate when possible, and avoid identifying reporters, operators, or uninvolved individuals beyond source necessity.

entries.topic: registry, preregistration, retraction, and post-publication critique records
entries.risk: Denominator-visibility records can be weaponized into researcher surveillance, blame, or misconduct implication; clinical-trial records may include sensitive medical contexts; private or embargoed preregistrations are ethically bounded.
entries.handling_rule: Treat platform records as source infrastructure only. Do not infer nonpublication, null results, misconduct, or study failure from absence, privacy status, or comments without independent source support. Future child records naming people must preserve context, status, source support, and correction/right-of-reply surfaces.

entries.risk: Audit records can be weaponized into simplistic claims that named researchers, sponsors, journals, fields, or therapies are dishonest or invalid.
entries.handling_rule: Frame records as evidence-system audits. Keep source, claim, publication status, outcome status, and motive separate. Clinical implications require current expert guidance and are outside this cube unless explicitly sourced.

entries.risk: Software incidents can expose sensitive personal data, financial disruption, medical/transport impacts, exploit pathways, or vendor/regulator blame incentives.
entries.handling_rule: Use public official/vendor sources with provenance labels; never include credentials, exploit steps, victim-level records, or unnecessary personal detail; preserve non-equivalence among vulnerability, breach, outage, and postmortem.

entries.risk: When software outputs are treated as evidence, harmed people can be blamed for hidden system state they cannot inspect; records can amplify stigma if written as scandal summaries.
entries.handling_rule: Encode attribution surfaces and evidence access; avoid claimant/patient/victim detail unless public-interest and source/ethics review require it; distinguish accident, institutional denial, and deliberate evasion.

entries.topic: multi-lab replication and living researcher dignity
entries.risk: Replication records can be misread as shaming original authors, entire fields, or individual labs; child records can amplify controversy without context.
entries.handling_rule: Frame records around claims, protocols, effect sizes, uncertainty, and source visibility. Include robust-control records and scope guardrails. Do not infer misconduct from non-replication. Preserve author responses only with source and context.

entries.risk: Clinical reversal records can be misread as current patient-specific medical advice or as condemnation of clinicians/patients who acted under older uncertainty.
default_handling: Every clinical record must state population, comparator, endpoint, and exception scope.
Avoid patient-specific advice and avoid hindsight contempt.
Distinguish source-backed reversal from guideline jurisdiction and from actual de-adoption in practice.
Preserve exceptions and boundary-sensitive subgroups as child-record obligations rather than erasing them.
